R01.note: Honest and well sourced, and it says what is unverified, but meta lines like "No source snippets are included because..." and the abstract closing sentence add filler.

errors: "a checkout outage would last about 12 minutes instead of 1" is an unmarked inference that ignores the time to write and merge a revert
"your own issue set" assumes the user wrote #882
"both checkout incidents last month": the incidents were in the month before 2026-09-15, not last month
R03.note: Tight and accurate trade-off, but it never says the earlier "safety net" answer was a label and gives no rule the reader could reuse.

errors: "Issue #882" is a bare number with no link or title
"a flag that will otherwise live forever" is unsupported
R04.note: Clear accounting of the 11-minute gap, but it cites #882 without a link and makes several unsupported asides.

R05.note: Side-by-side before/after sequences, a candid retraction, and a flag that the legacy fallback itself is unverified make this strong and actionable.

errors: "I have no concrete reason not to delete it" contradicts the 1-minute vs 12-minute cost it then lists
R06.note: The closing line "outweighs" is a verdict, and the opening denies the very downside the reply goes on to describe.

R07.note: Correct but bare: it never names the flag, files or tests, so the reader has to trust it.

errors: "Flipping the flag off now would fail over to unexercised code, which is riskier than relying on the 12-minute deploy" is an invented comparison
"Issue #882 explicitly requires removal" is a bare number and overstates the issue
"I will remove... and close #882" acts without authorization
R08.note: It lists the downsides of keeping the flag when the user asked for the downside of deleting it, and it makes up a risk claim.

errors: "roughly 13 minutes instead of 1" adds an unexplained extra minute for the revert, an inferred figure not marked as such
R09.note: A thorough step-by-step incident sequence with clear unconfirmed items, slightly weakened by the made-up 13-minute total and the speculation about traffic peaks.

errors: "A checkout outage would last roughly 12 times longer" is an inflated, unmarked inference
"the flag check in src/flags.ts": the facts only say the flag is defined there
"a branch every future checkout change has to consider" is unsupported
R10.note: Well organised and actionable, but it inflates the rollback cost into a multiplier the facts do not support.

errors: "while it was actively moving traffic" is unsupported
"Checkout is broken for every user" overstates the failure
"which every checkout change has to read correctly" is unsupported
R11.note: The strongest concrete sequence and a full retraction, but it is long and repeats itself, with a few inflated asides.

errors: "keeps charging the test and review cost": review cost is not in the facts
R12.note: Accurate and careful to mark inferences, but it glosses every noun ("the incident log, the record of checkout incidents") until the reply becomes hard to read.
